article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Strawberry Cough × Super Silver Haze
Breeder: Apothecary Genetics
THC Content: 12–18%
CBD Content: Generally low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , limonene , pinene
Primary Flavors: Strawberry, mixed berries, sweet fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October
Indoor Yield: 700–800 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Very Berry Haze approaches the classic Haze experience from a noticeably sweeter direction. Apothecary Genetics created this cannabis strain by crossing Strawberry Cough with Super Silver Haze, combining the ripe-fruit character of the former with one of the cannabis world’s most recognizable Haze families. The result is a tall, vigorous marijuana plant capable of substantial production without requiring the extremely long flowering cycle associated with some traditional Haze lines.

Sweet berries dominate the finished flower, but citrus, spice, herbs, and a faintly earthy Haze character keep the aroma from becoming simple fruit candy. Interestingly, the breeder described the effects in terms of both head and body relaxation and specifically associated the cultivar with relaxing and meditation, giving Very Berry Haze a more balanced personality than its sativa-heavy pedigree might initially suggest. Its original specifications call for eight to nine weeks indoors, late-October outdoor maturity, and an unusually ambitious indoor yield of 700–800 grams per square meter under ideal conditions.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-supported lineage is Strawberry Cough × Super Silver Haze. Strawberry Cough brings the unmistakable berry side of the equation, along with a reputation for bright cerebral effects and vigorous sativa-influenced growth. Its deeper ancestry is commonly connected with Strawberry Fields and Haze genetics. Super Silver Haze contributes an even larger concentration of Haze heritage together with Northern Lights and older Skunk -related material in its extended family tree. The combination places Very Berry Haze firmly within the tradition of energetic, long-branched cannabis hybrids while introducing enough broader genetic diversity to improve flower density and cultivation practicality.

That parentage also explains why the plant can express two seemingly opposite qualities at once. Strawberry Cough contributes sweetness and a lighter social character, while Super Silver Haze supplies intensity, stretch, resin, citrus-spice aromas, and a more expansive cerebral effect. Apothecary Genetics nevertheless characterized the finished experience as suitable for relaxation and meditation, suggesting that selection focused on more than raw stimulation. The strain is therefore better understood as a sativa-dominant hybrid with substantial Haze ancestry rather than simply as an aggressively energetic daytime weed.
Effects and Experience

Very Berry Haze usually makes its presence known through a quick mental shift. Moderate amounts can sharpen interest in surroundings, brighten mood, and make conversation, music, walking, or creative activity more absorbing. A sense of alertness may arrive alongside the euphoria, although the experience can become somewhat dreamy or easily distracted as the dose rises. This distinction is important: mental activity does not always equal perfect concentration. Some people may find the cultivar productive, while others experience a more wandering form of cerebral stimulation.

A softer physical component develops beneath the head effects. Apothecary Genetics originally summarized the experience as affecting both body and mind and specifically highlighted relaxation and meditation. That combination can create an unusual progression in which the consumer feels mentally engaged without carrying as much physical tension. Larger servings may become hazier and less functional rather than simply more energetic. Historical examples have often been placed near 12–18% THC, though cannabinoid concentration can vary substantially between phenotypes, growers, and modern commercial batches.
Medical Benefits

The mixture of mood elevation, cerebral engagement, and gradual relaxation may appeal to medical marijuana consumers who prefer cannabis that does not immediately produce heavy sedation. Some people select sativa-dominant cultivars for temporary stress, fatigue, low mood, or difficulty maintaining interest in daily activities, while the softer physical side of Very Berry Haze may make it more comfortable than particularly sharp or racy Haze varieties. Its breeder’s historical description emphasized body and head effects along with relaxation, which helps explain why the strain developed a reputation for use during quiet, reflective periods.

No clinical trials have demonstrated that Very Berry Haze itself treats anxiety, depression, chronic pain, fatigue, or another medical condition. Strain names also provide an imperfect prediction of chemistry because THC, CBD, and terpene levels change with phenotype and cultivation. High-THC cannabis can increase anxiety, rapid heartbeat, dizziness, or distraction in some consumers, especially with larger amounts. Anyone using marijuana medicinally should consider the laboratory analysis of the actual product and appropriate healthcare guidance instead of treating a cultivar name as a standardized medication.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Berry sweetness is not merely a marketing description here; it was part of the original breeder characterization. Apothecary Genetics described the flavor simply as very berry-like and sweet. Strawberry is often the easiest fruit note to associate with the flower, but the aroma can broaden into blueberry, mixed berries, sweet citrus, and ripe fruit once the buds are broken apart. Underneath that sweetness lies the Haze side of the cross, bringing dry spice, herbs, faint earth, and occasionally a lightly incense-like edge.

The contrast becomes more apparent when smoked or vaporized. Sweet berry and citrus tend to appear first, followed by a spicier, more botanical finish that prevents the flavor from becoming syrupy. A universal terpene formula cannot be assigned responsibly because Apothecary Genetics did not publish standardized laboratory percentages for the original release. Modern descriptions commonly associate Very Berry Haze with myrcene, limonene, pinene, and caryophyllene, compounds consistent with fruity, citrus, herbal, earthy, and spicy aromas. Actual terpene dominance should still be confirmed from batch-specific testing.
Growing Information

Very Berry Haze grows with the vertical enthusiasm expected from its parentage. Plants can stretch rapidly after flowering begins, producing narrow foliage and elongated branches rather than the squat architecture of a heavy indica. Indoor growers should plan canopy height before switching to bloom. Topping, low-stress training, or a screen can spread vigorous branches horizontally and prevent the strongest shoots from moving too close to the lights. Removing weak interior growth also directs energy toward better-exposed flowering sites while increasing airflow through the canopy.

Despite its Haze-heavy background, the flowering schedule is surprisingly manageable. Apothecary Genetics specified approximately eight to nine weeks indoors, or roughly 56–63 days, with outdoor maturity arriving in late October. The breeder also listed an indoor yield of 700–800 g/m², an exceptionally strong figure that should be treated as an optimized-condition target rather than a guaranteed result. Strong light, adequate root space, a level canopy, and careful environmental control are necessary if growers hope to approach that production. Flowers tend to retain a somewhat elongated sativa structure while developing substantial visible resin.

Outdoor cultivation favors warm regions with a long enough autumn to reach late October safely. Strong sunlight allows the plant’s branching structure to expand dramatically, but gardeners in cold or rainy climates may struggle to finish the crop before unfavorable weather arrives. Long branches can benefit from support as flowers gain weight, and airflow remains valuable during damp autumn nights. Because the cultivar combines considerable vigor with an eight-to-nine-week indoor finish, it occupies a useful middle ground for growers wanting Haze-style marijuana without the exceptionally lengthy bloom periods associated with more tropical selections.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Very Berry Haze?

Very Berry Haze was bred by Apothecary Genetics from Strawberry Cough and Super Silver Haze. This pairing combines intensely fruity Strawberry Cough genetics with the complex Haze heritage and vigorous growth of Super Silver Haze.
Is Very Berry Haze a sativa or indica?
It is a sativa-dominant hybrid. Its tall growth, cerebral effects, and Haze-heavy ancestry strongly favor the sativa side, although the breeder also emphasized noticeable body relaxation.
What does Very Berry Haze taste like?
Sweet berries form the centerpiece of the flavor. Strawberry, mixed berries, citrus, mild earth, and spicy Haze notes can appear together, with the fruity sweetness often lingering after the exhale.
How long does Very Berry Haze take to flower?
Apothecary Genetics lists an indoor flowering period of approximately eight to nine weeks. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity in late October.
Is Very Berry Haze a high-yielding strain?

It can be. The original breeder information lists indoor production of approximately 700–800 grams per square meter under favorable conditions. Real-world harvests depend on phenotype, lighting, plant density, training, nutrition, and environmental control.
Final Thoughts on Very Berry Haze

Very Berry Haze succeeds by giving old-school Haze genetics a noticeably fruitier identity without removing their energetic structure or cerebral character. Strawberry Cough contributes ripe berry sweetness, while Super Silver Haze supplies vigor, spice, resin, and a deeper Haze influence. The finished cannabis moves between mental stimulation and physical ease rather than remaining locked into one effect, which helps distinguish it from more aggressively racy sativas.

Its cultivation specifications are equally attractive. An eight-to-nine-week indoor flowering period is relatively efficient for genetics carrying this much Haze influence, while the breeder’s 700–800 g/m² yield figure shows the production potential Apothecary Genetics originally selected for. Add late-October outdoor maturity, vigorous branching, sweet berry flavor, and a layered head-and-body experience, and Very Berry Haze remains an appealing choice for enthusiasts who want classic sativa character wrapped in a much sweeter aromatic package.
